What Is Business Registration & Setup?

Business registration and setup is the process of choosing a legal structure (such as a Private Limited Company, LLP, OPC or proprietorship) and completing the registrations, licences and documents needed to operate legally in India. SLATOUT handles it end to end: structure selection, PAN, TAN, GST, Udyam/MSME, industry licences, trademark, and founder, HR and website legal documents.

Questions about Business Registration & Setup

Answers to what clients ask us most often about this service.

Ask us a question
01

What is the first step in registering a business in India?

The first step is choosing the right legal structure — sole proprietorship, partnership, LLP, One Person Company or Private Limited Company — based on ownership, liability, funding plans and compliance load. PAN, GST, licences and bank accounts all follow from that choice, so SLATOUT starts every engagement by assessing your activity and plans before recommending a structure.

02

Which is better for a startup: Private Limited Company, LLP or OPC?

It depends on your plans. A Private Limited Company suits startups that expect to raise equity funding or issue ESOPs. An LLP suits professional firms and partnerships that want flexibility and a lighter compliance load. An OPC suits a single founder who wants limited liability. We compare ownership, funding, compliance and tax implications before recommending one.

03

What documents are needed to register a company in India?

Requirements vary by structure, but typically include identity and address proof of directors and shareholders, passport-size photographs, proof of the registered office address and digital signatures for directors. After understanding your business, SLATOUT shares an exact checklist so you gather everything once, not repeatedly.

04

Do I need a trademark if I've already registered my company name?

Yes. Company registration protects your business name only for company-law purposes. A trademark separately protects your brand name and logo from being used by others in your industry. We run a trademark search first, then file the application and support objections and renewals.

05

Is GST registration mandatory for every business?

Not always. It depends on your turnover, the nature of your supplies and state rules, and some activities require registration regardless of turnover. SLATOUT checks what applies to your business and handles registration, amendments and cancellation. Thresholds and rules change, so we confirm against current law.

06

What registrations does an e-commerce or online business need?

Typically GST registration, Udyam/MSME registration, any industry-specific licences, and website legal documents such as a privacy policy, terms and conditions and refund policy. Marketplace sellers also need seller-account documentation. We map the exact list to what you sell and where you sell it.

07

Can you help after incorporation, or only with the initial registration?

Support continues after registration: licences, documentation, IP protection, business changes and closure as your business evolves. Ongoing GST return filing, reconciliation and tax compliance are handled under our Finance, Tax & Compliance service, so one team can support you from setup through operations.

What do technology and AI solutions for business include?

They cover websites and apps, business software such as CRM, billing, inventory and HR systems, workflow automation, AI chatbots and assistants, system integrations, and cloud and security support. SLATOUT builds only what solves a real business problem and connects it into one system rather than separate tools.

Do I need a full digital system, or just a website?

It depends on your stage. Many businesses start with a website, business email and Google Business Profile, then add a CRM, automation or AI as operations grow. We help you sequence the investment so you build what you need now and add the rest when it pays off.

Can you build AI chatbots or automation for my business?

Yes. We build AI chatbots, WhatsApp AI bots, lead qualification agents, customer support agents and workflow automation, each designed around a specific business problem such as slow response times or manual follow-ups, rather than added because AI is trending.

How can AI help a small business?

AI helps small businesses save staff time and respond faster: answering common customer questions, qualifying leads, drafting follow-ups, processing documents and automating repetitive tasks. The best use cases are repetitive, rule-based and high-volume. We identify those first, then build a practical solution around them.

What is business process automation?

Business process automation uses software to run repetitive tasks without manual effort, such as capturing leads, assigning them, sending reminders, updating records and notifying customers. It reduces errors and frees your team for work that needs judgement. We design the workflow, then connect your tools so it runs automatically.

06

Do you handle ongoing maintenance and security?

Yes. Cloud and server setup, backups, application security, performance monitoring and technical support are part of the service, not a separate add-on. Technology needs to stay reliable long after launch, so we keep it secure, monitored and updated.

What does an offline business launch service include?

It covers everything needed to enter a physical market with data instead of guesswork: market and customer research, location strategy and site comparison, competitor analysis and positioning, physical branding, and local launch and customer acquisition planning.

How do I check if there is demand for my business in an area?

Look at who lives and works nearby, what they spend, how many competitors already serve them and how those competitors are rated. We combine catchment mapping, local market visits, footfall observation, customer surveys and review analysis to estimate demand before you commit capital.

How do you choose the right location for a shop, café or clinic?

Do you help with store or outlet setup?

We guide the business-facing decisions: shop layout, customer entry and movement flow, display priorities, enquiry points, signage and physical branding. Is this service only for new businesses?

No. It also suits existing businesses expanding to a new locality, opening a new branch, or trying to understand why an outlet is underperforming. The same market, location and positioning analysis applies at any stage.

06

When should I start planning my local launch?

Before you sign a lease or commit capital. Location, pricing and positioning decisions made early are the hardest and costliest to reverse. If your location is already secured, we focus on positioning, branding and launch planning from that point.

Questions about Branding

Ask us a question
01

What is the difference between branding and marketing?

Branding defines who you are: your positioning, identity and voice. Marketing is how you communicate that identity to customers. Strong marketing built on a weak brand is expensive and forgettable. This service covers brand strategy, identity and offline marketing, with digital execution handled in Digital Marketing & Growth.

02

What is brand strategy?

Brand strategy is the plan that defines who you serve, what you stand for and why customers should choose you. It includes positioning, value proposition, audience personas, messaging, tone of voice and brand story, and it guides every logo, colour and campaign decision that follows.

03

How is a logo different from a brand?

A logo is one visual element of a brand. A brand is the full perception customers have of your business: its promise, personality, voice, visuals and experience. Designing a logo without positioning produces something that looks good but says little, which is why we start with strategy.

04

Do I need a full rebrand or just a brand refresh?

A refresh updates the visual identity when your positioning is still right. A rebrand rebuilds the strategy underneath it when your audience, offer or market has changed. We assess which you need before recommending either, so you don't pay for more change than necessary.

05

What is included in a brand style guide?

A brand style guide covers logo usage rules, colour codes (HEX, RGB, CMYK, Pantone), typography hierarchy, imagery and photography guidelines, co-branding rules and examples of brand voice. It lets anyone create on-brand materials consistently, long after the project ends.

06

Does branding include digital marketing or social media?

No. This service covers brand strategy, visual identity and offline marketing. Digital execution, including SEO, ads and social media management, is handled under Digital Marketing & Growth and built on the brand foundation created here.

A content strategy is the plan for what your brand publishes, for whom, why and when, created before any content is produced. It includes an audit, content pillars, voice guidelines, an editorial calendar and briefs, so every post, video and article supports a business goal.

02

What is the difference between content strategy and content marketing?

Content strategy is the plan: pillars, voice, calendar and briefs. Content marketing is the execution: writing, designing, publishing and promoting. Skipping the strategy usually produces inconsistent, off-brand content. SLATOUT separates the two so execution follows a clear plan.

03

What is a content pillar?

A content pillar is a core topic your brand consistently creates content around, such as a problem you solve or an area of expertise. Pillars help channels build recognisable authority instead of posting random, disconnected content, and they make planning far easier.

04

What is an editorial calendar?

An editorial calendar is a schedule showing what will be published, on which channel, in which format and when. It sets a realistic cadence, ties content to campaigns and prevents reactive, last-minute posting. Ours also maps each piece to a funnel stage.

05

How is content strategy different from SEO?

SEO focuses on helping search engines find and rank your pages. Content strategy decides what to create and why. They work together: our SEO content planning step uses keyword research and search-intent mapping so the content you plan is also content people are searching for.

06

Do you also post the content, or just plan it?

This service covers planning and briefing: the audit, pillars, voice guidelines, calendar and content briefs. Posting, scheduling and community management are handled under Digital Marketing & Growth. You can also take our briefs to your own writers, designers or agency and keep execution in-house if you prefer.

07

How often should I publish content?

It depends on the channel, audience and your capacity. Consistency beats volume. The editorial calendar sets a realistic, sustainable cadence for each platform, so you can keep it up rather than publishing heavily for a month and then stopping.

Ask us a question
01

How much budget do I need for digital marketing?

It depends on your industry, competition, goals and sales cycle. Instead of quoting a generic figure, SLATOUT builds a channel strategy and budget plan for your business, starting with the channels most likely to return leads or sales and scaling spend as results are proven.

02

How long does SEO take to show results?

Meaningful ranking movement typically takes three to six months, depending on competition, site health and content. Paid ads can drive traffic immediately while SEO builds in parallel, which is why we often plan both together.

03

Is SEO still worth it with AI search?

Yes. AI search experiences draw on the same fundamentals: useful, original content, clear structure and a technically sound site. SEO remains the base for visibility, and AEO and GEO extend it so your brand can also appear in direct answers and AI-generated responses.

04

What are AEO and GEO?

AEO (Answer Engine Optimisation) structures your content to give direct answers to questions, through FAQs and structured information. GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) builds your brand's authority so AI tools can understand and cite it. Both work alongside SEO; neither replaces it, and no one can guarantee inclusion in AI answers.

05

What is performance marketing?

Performance marketing is paid advertising measured on outcomes such as leads, sales or app installs rather than impressions alone. We run it on Google, Meta, LinkedIn and other platforms, tracking cost per lead, ROAS and ROI so spend is tied to business results.

06

Do you manage ad spend, or just strategy?

We handle it end to end, not just the strategy: channel selection, campaign setup, day-to-day execution and optimisation, and regular reporting. You can see exactly what each channel delivers, what each lead or sale costs, and where budget should move next to improve returns.

07

Which platform is best for my business, Google or Meta ads?

It depends on your product and how customers buy. Google captures people who are actively searching, while Meta builds demand and reaches people by interest and behaviour. B2B businesses often add LinkedIn. Recommending the right mix is part of our channel audit.

08

Do I need a website before starting digital marketing?

Not always, but a website or landing page significantly improves ad performance and conversion tracking. Without one you lose control of the customer journey and find it harder to measure what is working.

ACoS is ad spend as a percentage of ad-attributed sales. ROAS is the sales earned per rupee of ad spend. TACoS compares ad spend to your total sales, including organic. Together they show whether advertising is profitable, not just active. We report all three.

Decisions are made with profitability in mind rather than spend alone, and advertising is coordinated with your inventory so you don't pay to promote out-of-stock products.

Yes. We analyse catalogue quality, advertising, pricing, inventory and returns at SKU level to find what is holding growth back, then build a roadmap that scales your winning products and fixes or retires the rest.

Yes. We run consolidated multi-marketplace management covering strategy, catalogue, pricing, advertising and reporting across all your active channels. You get one view of SKU-level and marketplace-level performance instead of separate dashboards, which makes it easier to see where to invest next.

Questions about Programmatic Advertising

Answers to what clients ask us most often about this service.

Ask us a question
01

What is programmatic advertising?

Programmatic advertising is the automated, real-time buying of ad space across many websites and apps, using data to target the right audience for each impression. It covers display, video, connected TV (CTV/OTT) and digital audio ads.

02

How is programmatic different from Google or Meta ads?

Google and Meta ads are bought directly on those platforms. Programmatic buys inventory across the wider open web through a demand-side platform (DSP) using real-time bidding, giving reach beyond search and social, including streaming and audio.

03

What is a DSP (demand-side platform)?

A demand-side platform is software advertisers use to buy ad impressions across multiple exchanges and publishers in real time, with targeting, budgeting and reporting in one place. Choosing the right DSP for your goals and budget is part of our tool selection step.

04

What is real-time bidding (RTB)?

Real-time bidding is an auction that happens in a fraction of a second while a page or app loads. Advertisers bid for that single impression based on who the viewer is, and the winning ad is shown. It lets budget follow the right audience.

05

What is CTV advertising?

Connected TV advertising places video ads on internet-connected TVs and streaming apps. It combines the screen impact of TV with digital targeting and measurement, and it is one of the fastest-growing programmatic formats.

06

Do I need a large budget for programmatic advertising?

It works at various budget levels but is most efficient at moderate-to-large scale, because the technology and data targeting benefit from volume. We assess whether programmatic suits your budget before recommending it.

07

How do you protect campaigns from ad fraud and unsafe content?

Through brand safety and fraud-prevention settings, ad verification tools, frequency capping and inventory quality management. These reduce wasted impressions and keep ads away from unsuitable content, although no system removes risk entirely.

Questions about Finance, Tax & Compliance

Answers to what clients ask us most often about this service.

Ask us a question
01

What does your Finance, Tax & Compliance service include?

It is an integrated service covering accounting and bookkeeping, GST and income-tax compliance, audit and assurance, payroll, ROC and FEMA compliance, tax litigation support and virtual CFO and advisory services, all coordinated through one team.

02

How is this different from your Business Setup service?

Business Setup covers one-time entity setup: incorporation, registrations, licences and legal documents. Finance, Tax & Compliance covers the ongoing accounting, tax filing, audit and regulatory obligations once the business is operating, and continues for as long as the business runs.

03

What is a virtual CFO?

A virtual CFO is an outsourced finance leader who provides financial planning, budgeting, cash-flow management, MIS reporting and investor-ready analysis without the cost of a full-time CFO. It suits startups and growing businesses that need financial direction beyond bookkeeping.

04

What is the difference between bookkeeping and accounting?

Bookkeeping records daily transactions accurately. Accounting goes further: reconciling, preparing financial statements, analysing results and supporting tax and compliance. Reliable bookkeeping is the foundation; accounting and MIS turn those records into information you can use for decisions.

05

How often do GST returns have to be filed?

Regular taxpayers generally file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B monthly, while eligible small taxpayers may opt for the quarterly QRMP scheme, and an annual return (GSTR-9) applies subject to thresholds. Rules and due dates change, so we maintain a compliance calendar and confirm against current notifications.

06

Do you help with GST or income-tax notices?

Yes. We support scrutiny assessments, reassessment proceedings, rectification, refund follow-up, appeals and representation before tax authorities for both direct and indirect tax, from understanding the notice to preparing and filing the response.

07

Do you handle transfer pricing and international taxation?

Yes. We prepare transfer pricing documentation and benchmarking, analyse DTAA treaty benefits, review permanent establishment risk, and manage withholding tax, FEMA and cross-border compliance for businesses with related-party or international transactions, including support if an assessment or audit follows.

08

Is this service only for large companies?

No. It scales from basic accounting and GST support for startups to audit, transfer pricing, litigation and CFO support for established and international businesses. Many clients start with accounting and GST and add services as they grow.
